name: Loi fédérale sur la transparence des personnes morales (LETA — Federal UBO Register Act)
reference: Pending publication in SR; adopted 26 Sept 2025
supervisor: Federal Office of Justice + FINMA + MROS

articles.title: Purpose
articles.requirement: Creates a central federal register of beneficial owners of Swiss legal persons and arrangements to combat misuse for ML/TF and tax evasion, and to fulfil Switzerland's FATF R.24 + R.25 obligations.

articles.title: In-scope entities
articles.requirement: Swiss-registered companies (AG / SA, Sàrl / GmbH, partnerships, cooperatives), associations and foundations meeting threshold criteria, and trusts with a Swiss link (Swiss trustee, Swiss assets, or Swiss settlor). Listed companies and certain regulated entities may benefit from equivalence carve-outs.

articles.title: Definition of beneficial owner
articles.requirement: Natural person(s) ultimately owning or controlling the entity. Threshold: ≥25% ownership (direct or indirect) of shares / voting rights / profit entitlement, OR control by other means (board appointment power, contractual arrangements). Fallback: senior managing official where no UBO can be identified.

articles.title: Initial reporting obligation
articles.requirement: Reporting entities must file UBO information with the federal register at incorporation / first registration. Filing includes: name, nationality, date of birth, residence, type and extent of beneficial ownership, basis of control. Transitional period for existing entities (typically 18-24 months after entry into force).

articles.title: Refresh on material change
articles.requirement: Re-filing required within 30 days of any material change: change of UBO, change in ownership percentage crossing the 25% threshold, change in control arrangements, dissolution. Annual confirmation of accuracy required regardless of change.

articles.title: Reporting for trusts and similar arrangements
articles.requirement: Trusts with a Swiss link: settlor, trustee, protector (if any), beneficiaries (or class), and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control. Foundations: founder, board members, beneficiaries.

articles.title: Reporting persons within the entity
articles.requirement: Directors / managing officers are responsible for filing accurate and complete information. Internal procedures must enable the entity to identify UBOs from shareholders / nominees / control documentation. UBOs themselves must cooperate.

articles.title: Verification obligation
articles.requirement: Reporting entities must verify the accuracy of reported information using reliable independent sources: certified ID copies (passport / national ID), corporate registry extracts, trust deeds and amendments, shareholder agreements. Reliance on family declarations alone is insufficient.

articles.title: Document retention
articles.requirement: Supporting documentation retained for at least 10 years after the relevant UBO ceases to be beneficial owner or the entity is dissolved. Available for inspection by authorities + (where authorised) by FIs and DNFBPs for AML purposes.

articles.title: Register access — authorities
articles.requirement: Federal and cantonal authorities (FINMA, MROS, OAG, tax authorities, criminal prosecutors, sanctions enforcement) have broad access for the performance of their legal tasks. Logged + audited.

articles.title: Register access — FIs and DNFBPs
articles.requirement: Financial intermediaries (AMLA Art. 2) and (post-revision) in-scope advisers may access the register for AMLA CDD purposes. Per-query authorisation; logging; data-minimisation principle — access only what is necessary for the specific CDD task.

articles.title: Register access — foreign counterparties
articles.requirement: Foreign authorities access register data through mutual administrative assistance under existing tax + criminal cooperation channels. No direct public access from abroad.

articles.title: Non-public register
articles.requirement: No public access. Departs from the original EU AMLR public-register model in line with the CJEU Luxembourg Business Registers judgment (Case C-37/20 and C-601/20) which struck down public-access provisions on Charter Art. 7 + 8 grounds.

articles.title: Sanctions — non-reporting
articles.requirement: Criminal sanction for wilful failure to report, providing false information, or wilful failure to update. Fine up to CHF 500,000 for legal persons; lesser fines for negligence. Directors / managing officers personally liable.

articles.title: Sanctions — UBO non-cooperation
articles.requirement: Beneficial owners who refuse to provide information to enable accurate reporting may be sanctioned (administrative fine + civil consequences for the entity). Repeated non-cooperation may trigger reporting to MROS as a red flag.
